gloss: to issue (a check); to shake out; to sprinkle

definitions.gloss: to issue; to draw (a check or bill)
definitions.explanation: To issue a financial instrument such as a check, bill of exchange, or money order.

definitions.gloss: to shake out; to sprinkle; to scatter
definitions.explanation: To shake something out of a container or distribute by shaking.

examples.japanese: {小切手|こぎって}を{振|ふ}り{出|だ}す。
{銀行|ぎんこう}から{為替|かわせ}を{振|ふ}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I drew a money order from the bank.

examples.japanese: {百万|ひゃくまん}{円|えん}の{手形|てがた}を{振|ふ}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: A bill of exchange for one million yen was issued.

examples.japanese: {袋|ふくろ}から{塩|しお}を{振|ふ}り{出|だ}す。
examples.english: To shake salt out of a bag.

examples.japanese: {中身|なかみ}を{全部|ぜんぶ}{振|ふ}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I shook out all the contents.

examples.japanese: カバンの{中身|なかみ}を{机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}に{振|ふ}り{出|だ}して{探|さが}した。
examples.english: I emptied the contents of my bag onto the desk to search.

notes:
A compound verb combining {振|ふ}る (to shake/wave) and {出|だ}す (to put out). Sense 1 (financial) is the more commonly encountered meaning in formal/business contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {小切手|こぎって}を{振|ふ}り{出|だ}す: to issue a check
- {手形|てがた}を{振|ふ}り{出|だ}す: to draw a bill of exchange
- {為替|かわせ}を{振|ふ}り{出|だ}す: to issue a money order

RELATED EXPRESSION:
- {振|ふ}り{出|だ}しに{戻|もど}る: to go back to square one — from the board game すごろく, where {振|ふ}り{出|だ}し is the starting point

NOTE:
Not to be confused with {降|ふ}り{出|だ}す (to start raining/snowing), which uses a different kanji.
